title: What is an echo chamber?

explain.say: Shout in a big empty hall and your own voice bounces back to you. That is an echo. Online, something similar can happen with ideas. Look at the board. It is a loop, and it shows how an echo chamber forms.

explain.say: Now look at feed shows more. Apps use algorithms, which are sets of computer rules, to guess what will keep you watching. So Leila gets more videos praising that club. And see others vanish? Videos with other views appear less and less. Have you noticed your feed showing the same kind of thing?

explain.say: See feels like all agree? After a while, Leila thinks everyone agrees with her, and anyone who does not seems strange. That is an echo chamber: a space where you mostly hear your own views echoed back. Researchers still debate how strong this is online, but most agree it is worth watching for. Can you see how the loop feeds itself?

explain.say: To escape, follow people with different views, search for other sides on purpose, and talk to real people offline. Hearing other views does not mean you must change yours, but it makes your thinking stronger. Well done! Challenge: find one well-made video or article that sees a topic differently from you.

faq.a: An echo chamber is a situation, online or offline, where people mostly hear opinions that match their own, so their views get repeated back and seem to be what everyone thinks.

faq.q: How does liking posts shape my feed?
faq.a: Each like, share or watch tells the app what you enjoy. The app uses that information to choose what to show you next.
asks: Tell me about you like a post

faq.q: What is an algorithm on social media?
faq.a: An algorithm is a set of computer rules. On social media it ranks posts by what it predicts will keep you watching, often showing more of what you already like.
asks: Tell me about feed shows more
How do social media algorithms work?

faq.q: Why do different views disappear from my feed?
faq.a: If you rarely click on other views, the algorithm predicts you do not want them and shows them less. Your own follows and friend groups also narrow what you see.
asks: Why do I only see posts I agree with?

faq.q: Why is an echo chamber a problem?
faq.a: It can make people think everyone agrees with them, make other views seem strange or bad, and spread false ideas unchecked. Researchers debate how big the effect is, but hearing several sides helps everyone think better.
asks: Tell me about feels like all agree

facts: Internet activist Eli Pariser made the term "filter bubble" popular in his 2011 book "The Filter Bubble".
Studies of social media disagree on how strong echo chambers are; several find most people still see some different views, especially offline.
